newsitem.title: USA: Torotel has Q2 loss, sees Q3, Q4 profits.
newsitem.headline: Torotel has Q2 loss, sees Q3, Q4 profits.

text.p: Torotel Inc, which incurred a second quarter net loss, said on Wednesday it expects profitable operations in the third and fourth quarters and has seen no impact on sales or bookings from an investigation at one of its operations.

"Aside from any special charges incurred for the ongoing investigation into the testing discrepancies, consolidated operations should be profitable again in the third and fourth quarters," said Chief Operating Officer Christian Hughes in a statement.

As previously reported, during the quarter Torotel had discovered its Torotel Products unit in all likelihood failed to perform thermal shock testing as often as required, and inaccurately certified this testing occurred.
The company said it had voluntarily reported this to the U.S. Department of Defense and is actively participating in the current investigation.
"In the meantime, there has been no impact on sales bookings, which is a good sign," Hughes said in a statement.
Torotel said it will provide further information as it becomes available.

Torotel reported a loss for its second quarter ended October 31, 1996 of $200,000 or $0.07 a share after a restructuring charge of $257,000 and a charge of $32,000 from legal costs arising from an investigation of product testing at a division. Earnings from operations, before the charges, were $107,000.
Torotel makes switching power supplies and magnetic components used in commercial and military electronics.
